lines.text: Oh, wow, that sounds great. Thanks Katie.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Thanks.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So Hana, tell me, do you cook much?

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Yes, I always cook. I often cook with my roommate, and we always make Chinese of Japanese food. How about you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Well, I don’t really cook that often cause I’m really busy during the week, so I always just get something at the shop and eat that. But during the weekends, I always cook during the weekends because I really like making food, so that’s what I do.

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: So, do you ever eat out?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Only occasionally because I’m really busy during the week, and I prefer cooking during the weekends, so not really often. I don’t go out really often to eat, but whenever I’m tired, and I don’t have time to cook during the weekend, I go and eat out with a friend. So how about you?

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Well, I always , so I normally go and eat out during the weekend with my friends or family.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: So, do you ever buy take-away?

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: No, I never. Normally when I go out to eat, I like to sit and enjoy my food. How about you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Well, that's really nice. Of course, I do like to sit and enjoy my food, but I have to admit that occasionally I have to buy take-away, especially when I'm coming late from work, and I'm driving. I'm so hungry that most of the time, I don't really make it home, so I have to buy something and eat it on my way, and that's a shame, but that's the way it is.
And do you usually have people over for dinner?

lines.speaker: Hana
lines.text: Yes, I sometimes do. I really like cooking so occasionally I invite my friends over and cook for them or we all cook together. How about you?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Not really. I do love cooking, but the problem is my place is really small, so even though I want to invite my friends, I never do it because my place would only fit one or two people, so, unfortunately, I never have my friends over for dinner.

lessons.title: What is a typical day for you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So Natalie, what is a typical day for you? For example, what is a typical morning?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Well, I wake up at about 7.00 a.m.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh that's early.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes, I really am a morning person.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I think you are a morning person. I'm not a morning person at all.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Well, I don't actually get out of bed until about 7.30.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay, so what do you do?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Well, I play on my phone, I check my emails, I check Facebook, and I read the news.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you eat breakfast at home?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I usually prepare breakfast at home, yeah.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What do you eat?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Oh, just the simple stuff, eggs, bacon, sausages, sometimes I'll have toast.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you drink coffee or tea?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: No, I don't like coffee or tea.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, what do you drink?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Actually, I like hot chocolate in the morning.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I like hot chocolate too. So what about your day?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Well, I'm a teacher. I teach at a school. Lessons start at about 9.00 a.m. and we have lunch at noon.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: How many classes do you have in the morning?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Each class lasts an hour, so I have three classes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you eat lunch at school?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes, we have a huge canteen.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Is the food good?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: The food is great and it's so much fun eating with the students too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Is the food cheap or expensive?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: It's pretty cheap. I'd say maybe $3 for lunch.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh that's really good.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yeah, and for that you get a lot of food.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What do you do in the afternoon?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: In the afternoon I have more lessons, usually taking me till about 4.00 p.m.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh and do you have big classes?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes, so I teach English, that means I teach the whole year, so I have really big classes. We have about 200 students at the school.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's a lot.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes it is.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What about the evening? What do you do in the evening?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: When I get home I'm usually really tired, so I get changed into my pajamas and I watch TV for about two hours. After that, I'll maybe have some dinner, maybe get a pizza and then read a book or play on my phone again.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What do you watch on TV?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I really like watching Korean drama.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Korean dramas are cool.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I know, the characters are so much fun.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you listen to K-pop?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: A little bit but I think it's a little bit boring. I prefer American pop.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh so you like Korean dramas and American music?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: That's right. I also like game shows.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, what game shows?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Well actually my favorite one is Busted, and that's also Korean.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay, I need to see that. So when do you go to bed?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Most nights I go to bed at around 10.00 p.m. but at the weekend, sometimes it's later, maybe around midnight.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well I think you have an interesting and long day.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: That's right, I'm usually very tired.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Natalie, let's talk about our favorite things.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: First, what is your favorite color?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: My favorite color is purple.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really? My favorite color is purple, too.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, but I don't have purple clothing. I love the color purple, but I don't have purple clothes.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Oh, well, everything I wear is purple.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No kidding?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yeah, really.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's so cool. So, what about food? What's your favorite food?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Good question. My favorite food is pizza. I love pizza, but I don't like really big pizzas.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I love pizza, too. What is your favorite topping on pizza?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I like really spicy toppings, so salami or pepperoni, chilies, and sometimes bell peppers, too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you like thick pizza or thin pizza?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: No, I don't like thick pizza, because I can't eat too much. The thin pizzas, I get lots of toppings and I don't feel so full.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I agree. What about seasons? What is your favorite season?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: My favorite season is winter.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Winter?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yeah, I love winter, don't you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No, I hate winter. Why do you like winter?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I love the snow.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I hate the snow. Well, I like the snow a little bit, but I hate cold weather.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yeah, I guess the cold is kind of annoying, but the snow is so much fun. I go skiing and I play snowball fights and I build snowmen.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, that sounds fun. What about sports? What's your favorite sport?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I'd say my favorite sport is tennis.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's interesting. Do you play tennis?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yeah, but I'm not very good.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you like singles or doubles?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: At the moment I'm having singles lessons. They're really fun.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, now you are taking tennis lessons?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes, about twice a week.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you watch tennis on TV?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: Yes, I watch it all the time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Who is your favorite tennis player?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I really like Roger Federer.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. He's really good. Okay, last question. What is your favorite movie?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I don't have a favorite movie, but I really like comedies.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, what is your favorite comedy?

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: My favorite comedy is Ace Ventura.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ace Ventura is very funny, but that movie is really old.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: It is, but it's a classic, Todd.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It's like 20 years old, I think, maybe more.

lines.speaker: Natalie
lines.text: I know. I've seen it a hundred times.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I like it a lot, too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What is blue?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: The ocean is blue. The sky is blue. During the day, the sky is blue. And my eyes are blue.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, mine too. What is red?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Red. Let's see. Well, tomatoes are red. Strawberries are red, and ...

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: And roses are red.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Roses are red. That's right.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. What is green?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, lots of vegetables are green. Lettuce is green. Cabbage is green or purple. And asparagus is green.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Asparagus, right. Also, grass is green.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's right. Grass is green.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What is yellow?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, lemons are yellow. The sun is yellow, sometimes, or orange.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Or red.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What else is yellow?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sunflowers are yellow.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sunflowers are yellow. That's nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What is orange?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Also, sometimes the sun is orange. Oranges are orange.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Of course.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And persimmons are orange.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I know.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Carrots.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Carrots.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Carrots are orange.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Of course. Carrots are orange. What is black?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sometimes dirt is black. The night sky is black.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Right. And your shirt is black.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes. I like my black shirt.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What is white?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Vanilla Ice Cream is white. The snow is white.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes. And clouds are white.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Clouds are white. And sometimes clouds are black.

lines.text: Yes, when it's going to rain.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Or gray.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Right. What is pink?

lines.text: Some flowers are pink. Cotton candy is pink.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And, sometimes lollipops are pink.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. A lot of candy is pink, sometimes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Now, sometimes women's clothing is pink.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Or men's.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Or men's. Do you like pink shirts?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't usually wear pink shirts. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I don't like pink shirts. I don't like pink, actually.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, that's too bad.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What is your favorite color?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: My favorite color is orange.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really? Orange?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, I love orange. It's so bright. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I have three. I like the same. I know I like green. I love green, I love blue, I love purple.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: You like the cool colors.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Right. I don't like orange, I don't like yellow, and I don't like pink.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: You don't like the warm colors.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes. Bright colors, not so much.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What about red? Do you like red?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't especially like red. I like red poppies, a type of flower.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right, yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: But I don't like to wear red.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, me too. Do you dislike any colors?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Actually, I don't like brown. I think it's a boring color.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, that's true. But often dogs are brown and I love dogs.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I also like dogs, so a brown dog is okay. But a brown shirt, no, thank you.

lines.text: So Todd, where are you from?

lines.text: I am from the U.S., I am from San Francisco. It's on the west coast.

lines.text: And what do you do?

lines.text: And what does he do?

lines.text: He is also a manager, he works for a tree cutting company. They cut trees.

lines.text: Wow. That sounds exciting.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, cool job.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Is it dangerous?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is, a little dangerous. A little. And Aimee, what about you? Where are you from?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. And what do you do?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I'm also a teacher.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. What do you teach?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I teach English.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, me too.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: It's fun, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is. It is very fun. Excuse me, can I ask, how old are you?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Of course, you can ask. I'm 34.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Very young. Very young. Where is your mom from?

lines.text: My mum is also from Glasgow.

lines.text: Oh, nice. What does she do?

lines.text: Oh nice. And is your dad from Glasgow?

lines.text: Yes, he is.

lines.text: Oh wow. Many teachers.

lines.text: Yes. Looks like it.

lines.text: Well, thanks Aimee. Nice talking to you.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: You too, Todd.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Actually, I love cooking. I like to try new dishes and I love baking as well.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, nice. That's interesting. Because I hate cooking.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. And I don't know anything about baking, but I like cleaning. Cleaning is relaxing.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Really? Is that true?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Really, I like cleaning. So, my house is usually very clean.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: My house is usually clean also, but I don't like cleaning very much.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I think most people don't like cleaning. But some people think cleaning is relaxing. Like me.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That's true. What else do you like to do?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, I like exercising. I like going to the gym. I like listening to podcasts. So, I listen to a lot of podcasts a lot. I like surfing the internet. And sometimes, I enjoy reading books.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I also enjoy reading books when I have time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: But these days, I often listen to books instead. I listen to audio books.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I like listening to audio books.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Because I can exercise at the same time.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So, exercising and reading at the same time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, it's fun. So, I love jogging and I go jogging almost every day, usually for one hour. I listen to audio books when I jog.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So, you can do two things at once.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Very important. Multitasking. I love multitasking.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sounds like you're good at multitasking.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Let's talk about outdoor activities. Do you like doing yard work?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't especially like doing yard work. But right now, I don't have a yard. So, doing yard work isn't something I have to worry about. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I like doing yard work. I think it's very relaxing. It's like cleaning. So, I enjoy it. But like you, I don't have a yard. So, now I don't do yard work very much. Or I can't do yard work.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So, you like gardening if you have a yard?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I grew up on a big house. So, we have lots of yard work, lots of gardening. So, yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: But what about other things like hiking, do you like hiking?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I love hiking. Anything that is in nature, I love doing. I love hiking. I love kayaking. I love canoing. Any outdoor sports. Do you like hiking?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do. I'm with you . I love hiking. What about things like rock climbing?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have never been rock climbing. Have you gone rock climbing?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. Rock climbing looks dangerous. So, I'm still scared.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah,

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, I've never done rock climbing either. What about things like singing and dancing? Do you enjoy singing and dancing?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I enjoy singing, but I'm not very good at it. So, I like singing when I'm alone or in my car. Are you good at singing?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No, I'm terrible at singing. So, I hate singing. I really, really hate singing. But I like going to karaoke and listening to people sing.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, some people are really good at singing. What about dancing?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I hate dancing too. Yeah, I'm not good at dancing. So, dancing is very embarrassing for me. I don't like it.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I'm not good at dancing either .

lines.text: Are there any other activities you really dislike doing? Like for me, I hate writing letters. For example, I don't like writing thank you letters. I don't like writing anything with my hand. Typing is okay. I don't mind typing things, but I hate writing.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So, using your hand to write, you hate writing?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I like typing. Fingers is okay. Thumb is okay on the phone. I don't mind texting, I don't mind typing. I just don't like physically writing with a pencil or a pen.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. Pen or a pencil, like writing a letter.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Right. Because my writing is really bad, and it's hard to read. So, it's embarrassing.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I'm sure it's fine.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. How about you? For example, do you like iron in your clothes?

lines.text: I don't like having my clothes, but my clothes usually don't need ironing, so I don't have to worry about it too much. I don't like doing laundry. It's related to ironing clothes. lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I don't mind doing laundry if I go to the coin laundry, but I hate hanging my laundry out. I hate hanging out my laundry. It takes forever . I don't know why, you put it out, you take it back in, it just takes so much time.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That's funny. I'm kind of the opposite . I don't mind hanging out my laundry, because I like saving money, so I don't have to use money at the coin laundry.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Plus, you are helping the environment.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That's true. I like helping the earth.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I should change. Okay. Thanks Meg.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.text: I don't think I'm too bad at saving money. I look at prices a lot. I also buy a lot of things on sale, so I'm able to save some money.

lines.text: Do you use coupons or special offers ?

lines.text: Oh, okay!

lines.text: Yeah. I would say summer is a good time. But in England, there is not usually a good time because it’s raining almost every day. But if you want to go to the beach, probably summer is a good time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. What about the fall?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I mean, the fall is okay. Winter is good. Lots of people go to, go swimming on Christmas Day.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, I definitely want to go there.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yes. It’s a lovely place.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, Katie, let's talk about family.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: In your family, who is nice?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: In my family, I think my, my mum is really nice. She's always looking out for everyone. She always makes sure everybody is happy. And she's just really nice and kind.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow! That's great. Who is a funny person? Who is very funny?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I think in my family; my dad is very funny. But I don't think he knows he's very funny.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Alright. Oh, that's interesting. Now who is serious? Is anybody serious?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I don't think anybody is serious in my family.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No uncles or aunts?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Everyone likes to have a laugh. Everyone likes to have a good time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh that-

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Everyone is always joking.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, what I nice family.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: (laughs)

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. Who is very hardworking?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Ooohh. Well obviously , my mum is very hardworking. And she's always been very hardworking. She has to make sure that the whole family knows what they're doing. She has to make sure the whole family is ready for every day. Yeah, I think my mum is the hardworking one.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. Is anybody not hardworking? Maybe a little lazy?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Definitely me. (laughs) Definitely me especially when I was younger. I would never help with any of the chores in the house. I was definitely the lazy one.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I understand, I'm the same way. OK. Now in your family, who is very smart?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: My brother is really, really smart. He actually went to Oxford University.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Whoa.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah, he's very smart. But I didn't get any of that. My brother has all the smart genes .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, that's a good school. OK. Who is very fit?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Hmm... Well, my dad is a chef and-

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah. My dad makes really, really good food, so no one in my family is fit. We all eat too much food.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, nobody exercises a lot?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Not really.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, okay. Yeah, in my family, my dad is super fit .

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: (laugh)

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. In your family, who is talkative?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Oh, I keep saying my mum for all of these but my mum is definitely the most talkative. She talks to anybody who - even people who she doesn't know. She will talk to anybody, strangers on the street, people she meets at the bus stop. She talks to everybody.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's cool. Now, who is quiet?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Hmm, I think when he's meeting people for the first time, my brother is very quiet. He's very shy. He doesn't like speaking to new people a lot.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. Thanks a lot. Sounds like a nice family.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah. I think so too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So after Laos, where did you go?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: After Laos, I flew to Vietnam. And actually I took the bus into Vietnam.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes. And in Vietnam, I traveled from the north, from Hanoi, to Ho Chi Minh City. But because my time was so short, I could only spend one or two days in each city.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah! What city did you like the most?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I think I prefer Hanoi the most. The food, the street food is amazing. It’s a very lively city, lots of motorcycles and traffic so it reminded me of Nigeria where I was born a little bit.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh cool!

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And what did you do in Vietnam?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I spent time in Hanoi. I also went to visit Sapa, which has a lot of rice terraces . So these are mountains where they’ve planted rice fields. So the scenery, the view is really beautiful. And you also get to meet the native people, the local people there. So I enjoyed it.

And then from there I went to Hoi An, which is a very historical city, very beautiful night scenery by the river. And then I went to Ho Chi Minh City but I could only spend one night there before leaving for Myanmar.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. And then, how was Myanmar? What did you do there?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Myanmar was my last stop. And I didn’t have so much time there but I managed to go—but I managed to visit some of the places I really wanted to see like Yangon, Bagan, and Mandalay.
I would say that Bagan was the highlight. They had many temples from the past and just seeing that many of them, it was very impressive.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That’s fantastic.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So what country was your favorite?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: It’s hard to say. They each have their own good points but I think I would definitely like to visit Thailand again.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh OK. Thailand is such a great place. Anyway, thanks Abidemi.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Thank you, Todd.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Abidemi, what did you do for summer break?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: For summer break, I went to visit some countries in Asia.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, what countries?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I visited Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, and Myanmar.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, great. What did you do in each country?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: In Thailand, I was there for about a week. I ate a lot of delicious food and I met a lot of many nice people. I loved Thailand, so I hope to return again.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What foods did you eat?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I don’t remember the names but I just remembered that they were all good. (Laughter)

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Thai food is so good.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Did you go anymore in Thailand like the beach or the forest?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I was more interested in nature, so I traveled from Bangkok to Chiang Mai and Chang Rai, and I went trekking and rode elephants. So that was one of the highlights of my trip.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh nice. How long was the trek?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: The trek was about a day. It was a trek for 2, 3 hours but then we also stayed overnight in a community in the hills. And then the next day, we trekked for a little bit to come back to the city.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. So was Thailand the first stop?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: Yes. It was my first stop. It was supposed to be the shortest stop but I loved it so much that I spent more time there.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: After Thailand, where did you go?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: From Thailand, I moved on by land to Laos.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And what did you do in Laos?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: In Laos, I mainly was in the northern part of the country, and I went zip-lining .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh fun!

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: It was fun. So—

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So zip-lining is going flying from tree to tree ?

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: That’s correct. So that was about two days’ worth of zip-lining, and we stayed overnight in a big tree house.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, how fun.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: It was quite an experience .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Abidemi
lines.text: I really enjoyed it.

lines.text: Hey Todd, can I ask you a favor?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sure, anytime.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Um, I really need a place to stay, and I heard that your place is on AirBNB.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is on AirBNB. I do rent my house, but for you it's free.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OH, amazing. Can I stay there then?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: You can. How long?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Maybe a week or two weeks.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, when?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: From next Monday.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, actually, you can do that. That works.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Excellent. Thank you so much! How about a car? Can I park my car?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah, that's a problem. You can't park your car because there's no space, but there's a cheap parking lot about maybe two blocks away.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, it's only a couple dollars a day.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK, I guess I can park my car there. How about cooking there? Can I cook?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Of course, you can cook. I have a stove, a refrigerator. You can bring your own food. You can do whatever you want .

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Excellent. Thank you. Can I use the Internet?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: You can use the Internet. There's a password. I will write down the password before I leave, and I will write down the password before you get there.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Excellent. Thank you so much! I was thinking about asking my friend if he can stay. Can my friend stay over?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, sure, so your friend can stay. Not a problem I don't think.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: He has a dog? Can he bring his dog?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that is a problem. Does the dog have a cage?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Ah, no, but we can get a cage.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I'm not sure about the dog. If the dog is in a cage, it's OK in the house but I think you can't have the dog in the house.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK, how about smoking? My friend is a very heavy smoker . Can he smoke outside?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, he can smoke outside, just please pick up cigarette butts, but of course, he can't smoke inside.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK, he can't smoke inside.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK, how about if we want to have a party? Can we have a party?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, you can have a party. That's OK, but please be quiet. Don't be too loud. The neighbors live very close to my house.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Alright, that sounds good. Thanks. And I have one more question. Can I use the washing machine?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, of course. You can use anything. You use the washing machine. You can use the Internet. You can use the TV. You can use anything you like .

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Wow, excellent. That sounds great. Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I will write down directions for my house, and I will send you a map, and you can check it out and get all the information, and just I will leave the key for you with my neighbor.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Excellent. Thank you very much!

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sure, no problem.

lines.text: So Meg, are you busy this weekend?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes, I'm so busy because I'm moving.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, no.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, there's a lot of work to do.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What do you have to do?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: First, I have to prepare my apartment, so I need to pack all of my things.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's not fun.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No, it takes a long time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you need help?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, do you have time to help me?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I can help you on Sunday.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ooh, are you busy on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, on Saturday I have to work. I have to teach two classes, and then after I teach, I have to grade papers.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, it sounds like you're really busy, too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Plus, I have to meet my friends that evening.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, what will you do with your friends?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I'm helping my friend also. My friend has car problems , so I have to take him to the mechanic , but on Sunday I can help you.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: OK, that would be great because on Sunday I have to take some trash to the dump , and I have to finish some paperwork at city hall to prepare for moving to a new country

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Now, because you're moving, do you have to go to the post office?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do have to go to the post office. I almost forgot. At the post office, I have to submit a form to say my new address.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah, that's good because I have to go to the post office, too.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, really.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I have to send my mom's birthday gift to her.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: When is your mom's birthday?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It was one month ago.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ah, so you have to send it quickly.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes, I have to get on it .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: OK, well, let's go together.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, I'll see you Sunday. What time should I be here?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have to go to city hall by three p.m., so can you come at two?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, but if you want to go to the dump, the dump closes at noon, so we have to leave early.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ah, OK. Can you come at eleven?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes. OK, so I will see you at eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Great, see you then.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Bye.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Bye.

lines.text: OK, we'll talk about movies.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK.

lines.text: Have you ever seen a German movie?

lines.text: I haven't seen a German movie. I haven't seen very many movies.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, OK.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Even English movies, I haven't seen very many.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, have you seen a Canadian movie?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Uh, I don't know. Have I?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, the thing is , in Hollywood in America, all the famous actors are Canadian, so I think everybody's seen a Canadian movie.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I've definitely seen a Canadian actor.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, all actors in America are Canadian it seems like .

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I think so.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, have you ever bought something from Italy?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: From Italy. I have. I have bought - not for me - but I bought my mother a bag from Italy one time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, what was the brand?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I have no idea . She asked me to buy a brand and I bought it, but I don't know which one it was.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, have you bought something from Japan?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I've bought lots of things from Japan. I've lived in Japan for a few years, so I've bought all kinds of things from Japan.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, and now we'll move on to countries.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Have you ever been to France?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I have. Actually, I have been to France a couple of times. My high school has a house in France, so for our school trips we would go to France every year.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ooh, how nice.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah, how about you? Have you been to France?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: You know, I haven't really. I took a bus from England to Prague, so the bus drove through France, but it never stopped.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What other countries have you been to?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I've been to Germany, I've been to Hong Kong, I've been to South Korea, and I've been to China.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, you've been to a lot of places.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah. How about you? What countries have you been to?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah, I've been to countries in Europe. I've been to Israel. I've been to Cambodia, and Laos. I worked in Thailand, and I've been to Taiwan and Korea.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Wow. Which country did you like the best?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh boy ! That's impossible. I will say this, I love ... I love Seoul. I love Seoul, Korea. It's a great city. OK, anyway , thanks Katie.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.text: OK, Katie.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.text: Let's take an international test.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Oh, OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: How international are you? Let's find out .

lines.text: Let's find out.

lines.speaker: Katie

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, is that Greek?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I think so. I've had that, but apart from that , I've never eaten Greek food. How about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah, I think I have. Like, I've eaten Greek yogurt. Does that count?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: That counts.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That counts?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: That counts.

lines.text: OK, have you ever eaten Vietnamese food?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Ah, I see it written down. Is it pho?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Pho, the noodles?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah, I've eaten pho before.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I've been to Vietnam so I've eaten Vietnamese food a lot. And pho the noodles is really good.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Yeah, it's delicious.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I've had that too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, OK. Have you ever studied French?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I have. I studied French for five years.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, can you still speak French?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Nope . Not at all .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, me too. I once studied French years ago, but I haven't spoken French in so long I can't remember anything.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I can't remember anything either.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Have you ever studied an Asian Language?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I've studied Japanese. I can still speak it a little bit now, and I studied a little bit of Korean, but I don't speak Korean.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, really. OK. Wow, like I've studied Thai because I lived in Thailand for five years, and like you I've studied Japanese, but my Japanese is terrible.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: How about your Thai?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: My Thai is OK. It's OK. I can talk a little bit. OK, so have you ever met a Spanish person?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: A Spanish person? Actually, I don't think I have.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I don't think I have met a Spanish person.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, interesting. I've been to Spain so, I've met a few and we have a Spanish teacher at our school.

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Oh, maybe I have met a Spanish person then. Maybe, I've met a secret Spanish person.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, have you met a Chinese person?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: Oh, yes, I've meet lots of Chinese people.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, and have you met a Brazilian person?

lines.speaker: Katie
lines.text: I feel like if I say no, then I have. Probably. Probably, I've met a Brazilian person.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I've met a few people from Brazil, so they're alway very nice. Very friendly people.

lines.text: So Aimee, let's talk about routines?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What time do you get up most days?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I get up ... I get up about six.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, wow! That's early. I'm about the same. I get up at 7ish, usually.

lines.text: OK, and what do you ear for breakfast?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I usually have toast. I'm lazy. I don't cook in the mornings, so toast, but I always have coffee

lines.text: Right. Yeah, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I love coffee. Do you have coffee every morning?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I have coffee every morning. I also have hot water and fresh lemon juice, every morning.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Because it is good for your body, and I enjoy it.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK. Good. So when do you leave the house most days?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I leave the house about seven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, that's early.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: It is. Maybe between seven and seven-thirty. Yeah. How about you Todd?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: A little later, usually around 8.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK.

lines.text: And where do you eat lunch every day?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Every day? I eat lunch at work every day, so I will buy something from the cafeteria at my work, or I will bring something

lines.text: Most days, what do you have for lunch?

lines.text: I have a sandwich and a smoothie.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Mm, that's healthy.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: You're healthy.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: No, not really. (laughter) Yeah, sandwich and a smoothie and probably a chocolate biscuit.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ooh, OK. That's not healthy.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: It's not. And you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I eat at the cafeteria every day at my school and I always have salad every day. I love salad, yeah! I usually have a very healthy lunch. I have lean meat. Chicken usually and a salad and tea.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: That does sound healthy.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is, kind of. A healthy meal of the day.
So, every day, who do you talk to?

lines.text: I talk to my children every day. Yes, we talk a lot.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What do you talk about?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: We talk about our everyday routine. I remind them to do their tasks, and I remind them to get on with ...

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: the chores ?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yes. Chores and their routine.

lines.speaker: Todd

lines.text: Well, they're still young, so my two-year old doesn't do anything. She brings her plate to the kitchen when she's finished. She's good at that actually. My eight-year old, she folds her clean laundry and puts it away

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's good.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. Very responsible. So when do you get home most days?

lines.text: I get home around six o'clock. How about you Todd?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I get home late. I get home around ten o'clock.

lines.text: Oh, that is late.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, very late. So I work late. I live alone so, I work late and I go to the gym and sometimes I go eat at a restaurant.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I never cook.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I never go to the gym.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: (Laughter)

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: (Laughter) What time do you go to bed then?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I go to bed early actually. I get home at nine or ten and I go to bed by eleven usually. And you?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Eleven's early.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is early.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK, I think I'm probably about the same. Eleven o'clock. Yeah, I go to bed about eleven o'clock.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: OK, so how many hours do you sleep most nights?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I guess I get about seven. Six or seven hours.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I get eight. I love sleeping.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: You sleep more at the weekend?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Hmm! You sleep in Saturday and Sunday?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I try if I can.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sunday is easier to sleep in.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK, thanks Aimee.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Hey Aimee, how are you today?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: I'm good, thanks Todd. And you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I'm good. Pretty good. Let's talk about your favorite things.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What is your favorite food?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Ooh! My favorite food is avocado.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Avocado?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Honestly .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow!

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: How about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: My favorite food is pizza, I think. I love pizza.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Oh, me too!

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It's so good.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: It's so delicious.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: And what is your favorite movie?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, my favorite movie is Star Wars.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Classic !

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I know. And you? What is your favorite movie?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Well, I do love Star Wars too, but my favorite movie Ferris Beuller's Day Off.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ooh! I like that movie a lot. Very good. Very good. So I was in high school the same time as the movie

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Were you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah !

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Great!

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So cool. Who is your favorite actor?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: My favorite actor is Jean Reno.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Hmm, the Frenchmen.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yes. Yes, he's French, but he's been in a lot of American movies too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, I like the movie Leon.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Love it!

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It's very cool.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yes, I agree. How about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: My favorite actor is Brad Pitt, so I like Brad Pitt a lot.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: He's great.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, he is good.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Very talented.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah, who ... I'm sorry ... what is your favorite season?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: My favorite season is probably Spring. I think. It's ... the cool of winter has passed and it's not too hot yet, so I think Spring. How about you? What's your favorite season?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, my favorite season is the Fall or Autumn. I love the Fall. I love the colors. It is not hot. It is not cold, and they are many holidays, and my birthday is in the Fall.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: They are great reasons to love Autumn.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So, when is your birthday?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Actually, my birthday is also in Autumn. My birthday is in October.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, wow! Me too. My birthday is also in October. What day?

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: 14th!

lines.text: And you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: The second. Cool! So next year let's have a birthday party together.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: OK.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: October birthday party.

lines.text: Good idea .

lines.text: So what is your favorite city?

lines.text: Oh, in Japan.

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: Yes, yes. So far. Yes, Osaka is very noisy and colorful and the people are very open and talkative, so I really enjoy Osaka.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice .

lines.speaker: Aimee
lines.text: How about you? What's your favorite city?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I think my favorite city is Barcelona.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, it's very nice.
