lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hey, Todd. Are you healthy? Do you eat lots of fruits and vegetables?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I guess I am healthy. I do eat lots of fruits and vegetables, but I also eat junk food, sadly . But I try to eat lots of fruits especially to stay healthy.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What kind of fruits do you like to eat?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, I like all fruits. I love all fruits except pineapple. I hate pineapple. I don't know why. I just don't like pineapple. I don't like the taste. I don't like to chew it. It just feels funny . But I love apples, I love bananas, I love oranges. I usually have an apple every morning for breakfast. It's very easy to eat. And I just love apples because you can take them to school. You can eat them quickly. They're very easy to eat.

I also like oranges, and I love orange juice. So sometimes, I make fresh orange juice in my kitchen. So oranges are great. But my favorite fruits are bananas and strawberries. I love bananas and strawberries. And I love to eat bananas and strawberries together, so my favorite snack is to cut up some banana and then cut up some strawberry and mix them together, and then eat them.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, it sounds like you really a lot of fruits.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh yeah, I do.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What about vegetables? Do you eat vegetables everyday?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do. I try to have a salad everyday, and I have a special salad I make and I call it my chunky, crunchy salad. And it's carrots, cucumbers and tomatoes, and I cut the carrots and cucumbers into small little squares. And then I cut up the tomatoes and I mix together. And the carrots, tomatoes and cucumbers mixed together, the colors are really pretty. And when you eat the salad, it's very crunchy and it's very chunky because it's all little squares. So I call it my crunchy , chunky salad.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That sounds delicious. Do you ever share it with someone else?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No, I don't but I want to because I really, I like it so much and I can't cook. So when I go to somebody's house and I need to bring food, I think, "Oh, I should bring chunky, crunchy salad."

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, that's a good idea. Another idea is to cook some vegetables. Do you cook vegetables?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Not too much. I do cook asparagus . Asparagus is probably my favorite vegetable, and it's very easy to cook because asparagus, you just have to cut up into small pieces. And then you can put the asparagus in a bowl with some water in the microwave, and you can cook asparagus in about 30 seconds. So I eat asparagus a lot.

Also, I eat broccoli. I love broccoli. Sometimes I have broccoli and lettuce together for my salad. And then sometimes, I cook eggplant. I like to cook eggplant because I like the taste and it's easy to cook.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't really like eggplant.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh no. Why not?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It has a strange flavor to me, so I prefer not to eat eggplant.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, as long as you eat your veggies .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So Meg, you look like a healthy person. Do you eat lots of fruits and vegetables?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do eat lots of fruits and vegetables, especially fruit. I love to eat fruit because it's so sweet.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah? What fruits do you like?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I love bananas because they're so healthy for you. And so usually, in the morning for breakfast, I'll have a banana. I also love blueberries. Blueberries are my favorite fruit. But sometimes, they're expensive so I can't often eat blueberries.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I agree. Blueberries are so good. I love blueberries in oatmeal.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That's a good idea. I love to have blueberries in muffins .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's nice. Well, you bake. Do you bake blueberry muffins?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do bake blueberry muffins, and also blueberry bread, blueberry pancakes, many blueberry things.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow. That's great. So are there any fruits you don't like?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't like kiwi actually because the flavor is okay but the fruits is too soft. So usually, I don't want to eat kiwi.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh well, I love kiwi. I love kiwi and bananas. It's very good.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, sounds okay but maybe I'll just have the banana.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So what about vegetables? Are you a person who eats lots of salad?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't eat a lot of salad but I do like to eat vegetables with my meals, usually lunch and dinner.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So you cook vegetables.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I cook vegetables or I eat vegetables fresh. For example, usually with my lunch, I'll cut up a cucumber, and put some salt or pepper on the cucumber and eat with my lunch.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh great. I love vegetable sticks , so I love carrot sticks, cucumber sticks, radish sticks. It's very good.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Do you like to dip vegetable sticks into any dressing?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do but it's not healthy, right?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: But yeah, I love the dressing like the ranch dressing with carrot sticks or the ranch dressing with cucumber sticks. It's very nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. It's pretty delicious. But you're right. Not so healthy.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. So what vegetables do you cook?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sometimes I cook broccoli. I actually like to roast broccoli, which is when you put broccoli into the oven and cook it a few minutes. So it's really delicious. You can add some salt or seasonings and it's easy to make. You can cook some meat or rice while the broccoli is in the oven and then it's ready for your dinner.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: That's great. Yeah. You see some vegetables like on a kebab that are roasted. I guess onions are roasted, peppers are roasted.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Right, right.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you roast other vegetables besides broccoli?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sometimes tomatoes, and sometimes potatoes although, it's that a vegetable.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is but it's not a very healthy vegetable.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So maybe I shouldn't eat potatoes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I love potatoes though. So you roast vegetables, do you cook vegetables any other way? Do you boil vegetables or fry vegetables?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sometimes I boil vegetables. For example, I like to boil carrots because they're soft and you can add some spices again to have some flavor when you eat carrots with your meal.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Actually, I love carrots but I only like raw carrots.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And I hate cooked carrots.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh well, I'll try to remember that if ever you come over for dinner .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Carrots sticks please.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hey, Todd. I noticed that you only have two pairs of pants.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh no. Really? Yeah, yeah. You got me. I have only two pairs of pants for work. I have my green slacks and my black slacks, and that's it . I don't like to buy clothes and I travel a lot, so I really don't have that many clothes.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Are you not into fashion?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I'm not into fashion. I'm not really interested in clothes or shopping. And I only have clothes for the season. And after the season, I usually throw the clothes away.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. So to save money, I don't buy a lot of new clothes each year.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. So you only have clothes for the season.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, what clothes do you usually wear in summer?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, summer is great because you don't need a lot. In summer, I just have four or five t-shirts. I usually have some white t-shirt or, you know, a blue t-shirt which has some letters on it or maybe a little bit of English. But usually, my t-shirts are really simple. And then I have some jeans, usually two pairs of blue jeans, and I have shorts for doing sports or running or exercising. I have four or five pairs of shorts. And that's about it.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, since you do some exercising, do you also wear sneakers?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do. I always have two pairs of sneakers. So I have one pair of sneakers for the gym, and then I have one pair of sneakers for just walking around town, and also for running, for jogging. So I have my outdoor sneakers and my indoor sneakers.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What about flip-flops?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I'm not a flip-flop guy. I do have a pair of flip-flops for the beach or for going to the store quickly, but I usually prefer to wear my sneakers.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: In the summer, it's so hot, I usually like to wear tank tops but I have to put on sun-block. What about you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do have to wear sun-block. I have very pale skin , so sun-block is very important. I should wear it more often, but I do have a hat, so I always wear my baseball hat in summer. So to protect myself from the sun, I just wear my hat all the time, and sometimes, sun-block.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So those are the clothes you wear in summer. What do you wear in winter?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: In winter, I'm also pretty basic. Each year, I usually buy a couple of new dress shirts, long-sleeve dress shirts that go with my slacks that you see at work. And that's about it. The only clothes I always keep, I always save are my nice jackets. I have two nice jackets for work, and I wear my, you know, my business jackets to school. And that's about it.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It does get really cold in winter. When you go outside, do you wear anything extra?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. I don't like scarves and I don't like things like ear muffs and gloves. So I usually just keep my hands in my pockets. But I do have a couple of sweaters. So each year, I like to buy one or two new sweaters. And I do wear those sometimes.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sweaters are warm. What about when it snows? Don't you wear boots?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. I don't wear boots. And luckily, it doesn't snow that often where I live, so I don't have boots. But I should buy some, maybe. Sometimes, I buy the really cheap rubber boots or plastic boots that I know I don't have to keep for a long time. But, you know, boots like that are easy to get rid of.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Do you ever wear something like long johns?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: You know, when I was little, I wore long johns . I grew up on a farm and it was very cold. But now, not so much. I don't wear long johns. But I do have sweat pants, so I have sweat pants and the sweat shirt for exercising in winter. I usually have two or three sweat suits like that. And sometimes, I wear those to bed.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, that sounds like a good idea. So summer, winter, what do you wear in fall and spring?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, fall and spring is great because in fall and spring, you can wear nice clothes. So usually, if I buy dress shoes, I like to wear those in fall and spring. In winter, sometimes, the dress shoes aren't really good for the snow but I like to wear nice dress shoes in the fall and spring.

And then, sometimes, in the fall and spring, I might wear a tie when I go to work. And of course, I have my slacks and I have my jeans, and I have my, you know, running shoes. So I keep those as well.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: As a woman, I often wear skirts. And so, sometimes in the fall and spring, I wear tights underneath the skirts but you don't wear tights, do you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No, I don't. Although, these days, when you go to the gym, they have special tights now for men that you can wear when you exercise. So there's like the running gear is almost like tights. It looks almost the same.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow, that's interesting.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, kind of strange.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So for any season, do you wear any accessories?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. I'm not a big accessory person. Like I said, sometimes, I wear a tie, but not often. And of course, I have a belt. I need a belt, but I have one belt, and that's it. But I don't like things like necklaces or, you know, bracelets. I don't really like jewelry. I do wear a watch sometimes but I don't wear a watch everyday because now, you don't need a watch. You can just look at your phone.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That's true. I usually use my phone also.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So Meg, we are talking about clothes, and you always look nice at work. You have a very nice fashion sense .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, thank you.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So you must go shopping a lot.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do go shopping sometimes. It's fun to go shopping and buy new clothes especially when it's a new season.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Like what do you like to wear per season? For example, what do you like to wear in winter?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: In the winter, it's pretty cold. So I like to wear sweaters. Sometimes, a t-shirt with a sweater over it to stay warm. Lots of long-sleeve shirts. I like to wear long-sleeve shirts. And I still wear skirts in the winter. So sometimes, I wear tights underneath the skirts to stay warm.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: What about dresses? Do you like to wear dresses?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do like to wear dresses. In the winter, it's a good time actually to wear sweater-dresses. They're warm and a dress, so it's nice for work.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Sweater-dresses.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Have you seen a sweater-dress before?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I have no idea what a sweater-dress is. What is a sweater-dress?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It's a dress but made of sweater material.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Ah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So sweater-cloth made into a dress. So it's very warm.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. I was picturing a sweater with a skirt attached to it.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: [Laughs] You might find that but I think a sweater-dress is a little different.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. What about… What about in the summer?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: In the summer, I love to wear flip-flops. It's my favorite thing to wear. So I often wear flip-flops with jeans or shorts, skirts again. I don't wear tights in the summer because it's too hot.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Right. Do you wear flip-flops to work?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I can't wear flip-flops to work. So when I go to work, I often wear high heels or flats, some dress shoes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. So do you like to wear shorts or skirts. Which do you prefer?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I prefer shorts because it's more comfortable and easy to move around. But I also can't wear shorts to work. So I have many summer skirts for work.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Now, let's talk about shoes. So women often have many types of shoes, high heels, boots, flats, like you just said, sneakers. So what kind of shoes besides flip-flops do you like to wear?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do have many pairs of shoes and so I like to wear flats and sandals especially in the summer. In the winter, I like to wear boots and rain shoes when it rains or rain boots. When I'm exercising, I like to wear sneakers or tennis shoes because it's good for your feet.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh right. Now you travel a lot, we both travel a lot. What shoes do you usually take when you travel?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: When I travel, I usually take flats because they're easy to remove at the airport and they're light and convenient for traveling.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, right.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What shoes do you usually use?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Just my sneakers. So my sneakers I wear everywhere. Now, women sometimes have accessories , you know, like earrings, necklaces, scarves, things like that. What do you like to wear?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I like to wear necklaces especially long necklaces. I don't like necklaces that are too short. It feels uncomfortable. I don't like to wear bracelets or a watch because I don't like anything on my wrist , but I do love to wear rings. I usually wear one ring each hand, just for fashion, not for anything special.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh that's nice. Cool. Well anyway, thanks, Meg.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Thank you.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So Meg, we are talking about animals; do you like to go to the zoo?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I love to go to the zoo.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. So when you go to the zoo, what animals do you like to watch?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I really like to watch giraffes. Giraffes are so tall and giraffes look really soft and friendly, so I wish that I could touch a giraffe someday.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's so true. There is a zoo near my house in California, and you can walk up some stairs and then you can feed the giraffes, and their face is the same height as your face, and they look really, really cute. Yeah, giraffes are great.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Giraffes are so cute. Maybe someday, I can feed the giraffes.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I like how giraffes look. I love their face. And I also love camels, also because I think camels have a similar face. They look really cool.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't think camels are very cute.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. They're so hairy. Camels have so much hair that they look ugly.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh really. I like camels. They always look cool and relaxed.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: They do look relaxed, but I like giraffes better than camels.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, what about llamas? Llamas are kind of like camels and they're kind of like giraffes. They kind of have the same face. Do you like llamas?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I think llamas look cute but I've heard that llamas aren't very friendly.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Have you heard about llamas spitting at people before?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No. Actually, I think I heard camels do that but maybe llamas do it, too.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. So what about other animals? What other animals do you like at the zoo?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I really like the zebras because zebras are black and white with stripes. So the zebra stripes are really cool, and zebras are similar to horses. So sometimes I think I could ride a zebra if I had one.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. That would be cool. Zebras do look pretty cool. Are there any other animals?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, there's one animal that I'm afraid of, and that's a bear.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, bears are pretty scary.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Bears are really scary and they're so big with huge teeth and giant claws , and I feel like a bear would eat me if I met it in person.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Actually, have you seen a bear in the wild ?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No. I have never seen a bear in the wild, and I really don't want to.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, in California, sometimes you can see bears in the wild, small black bears. And actually, the black bears are not that dangerous.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I mean, you need to be careful when you see a black bear in the wild, but they almost never attack anybody. So the one animal you must be afraid of though, is the mountain lion. So there are mountain lions also in California, and they are scary.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, so maybe I should avoid mountain lions, too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. If you walk in the wild and you see a mountain lion, maybe it's too late. You're already in trouble .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Maybe I'll just keep going to the zoo.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: [Laughs]

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hey, Todd. Did you have any pets when you were a kid?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I did. I had many pets actually. I had a dog, of course, and I had some cats. But actually, I grew up on a farm. Yeah. So we raised lots of animals, and on the farm, I always felt like the animals were my pets. So it was pretty cool.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. That sounds really exciting for a kid.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, it was great. It was the best.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What kind of animals were on your farm?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: We had almost every, you know, farm animal possible. For example, we had pigs. We raised a lot of pigs. And pigs actually are really good pets. They're very fun. Pigs are very friendly animals and they're not really dangerous, so… Also pigs like people.
So sometimes when we were little, we would ride on the pigs' backs but if our grandpa saw us riding on the pigs, he would yell at us. We always got in trouble .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Uh-oh.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Also, aren't pigs dirty?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: They are dirty. So when you would go in the pig pen , you would get very, very dirty. But, you know, when you are small, when you are young, you don't care. It's just fun.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: What about other animals like chickens?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: We did have chickens and lots of chickens. And the chickens maybe were the least friendly animals. So chickens don't like people.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And the chickens – you have to go get the eggs. So working with chickens was not easy, and I never liked the chickens that much. Plus, the chickens you eat more often, so it's a little different.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Right, yeah.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. I don't think I've ever seen a chicken in person .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh wow. You must be a city girl.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I am. Although, when I was young, I always wanted to have a horse. Did your farm have horses?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: We had one horse for a while, and then we had a pony. So yeah, we had one horse and we had one pony. The pony was great because when I was little, we could ride the pony but the pony was actually really mean. So the pony would bite you if you were not careful. And if you try to ride the pony, sometimes the pony would get angry, very angry. But it's okay. You know, when you're small on a farm, it's normal.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, that pony sounds scary. Were there any other animals that you had that were more friendly?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Actually, the best pet you can have is a goat.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Really? A goat?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Goats are fantastic. Goats love people. They really, really love people, and they're very social. And goats follow people. So when you are little on the farm and when you walk around, the goats become your friends.

So when I was little, I would walk and I had friendly goats that would follow me everywhere. And they were great, and they're very curious. They like to see what you're doing. Yeah. And they like to be petted. So, you know, like how you pet a dog, you pet a cat; goats also like for you to pet them. They're very, very social.

And it's interesting because goats and sheep are kind of similar but really, they're very different. So goats are very social . Goats are very friendly and sheep are very shy. And sheep don't like people at all. So sheep stay away from people and goats always get close to people.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hmm, sounds like a goat is a good pet to have.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Goats are the best. They are so friendly. And goats are cool because goats talk to you. So they like to make a sound. You know, like, "Baa-a!" They "baa-a" or whatever, they make a sound. And when you walk around as a young boy or young girl, the goats are great. They follow you and you feel like the goat is talking to you, which is cool.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: That sounds really fun. Now I wish I had some goats.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Oh, you got to. The only other animal we had – we also had cows.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And cows are cool. Some cows are friendly. Most cows are shy. But cows, you know, they always come to you because they think they will get food. But if they see you have no food, then cows stay away. So cows like sheep are a little afraid of people, but pigs and goats love people and they're very social .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, it sounds really cool, growing up on a farm.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It was. It was. I was lucky.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hey, Todd, where do you live?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I live on the east side of downtown

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh. Do you like it there?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do. I live in an older house. But it's a big house, and it's really relaxing. It's a nice place to live.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. Sounds nice. How many rooms does it have?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: My house is pretty big. It's four rooms. It has a big sleeping room. It's a Japanese house. So it's not really a bedroom because you sleep on the floor.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: But it also has a living room. It has, like, an office room and it has a kitchen.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Is it a big kitchen?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: No, it's a pretty small kitchen and it's a very old kitchen. I have a small stove . So it's very difficult to cook. But, you know, I have a refrigerator . I have a microwave. I have a nice kitchen table to eat at. So it's a pretty decent kitchen.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It sounds okay. What about your living room? What do you have in the living room?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: My living room, it's pretty cool for a guy because it's a good place to watch sports. I have a really big TV, and I have cable TV, so I get all the football channels.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Nice.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And I have a really big sofa, so I can sit on my sofa and watch sports and drink beer. It's great.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Sounds relaxing.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Very relaxing.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, do you also have a nice bathroom?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I do. I actually have three bathrooms.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It's kind of crazy, yes. So in English, we say bathroom, but I have two rooms that are for the toilet and I have one room or the bathroom with the toilet for the guests. And then I have a bathroom that I used. And then also I have a natural hot spring bath outside my house. So if I want to take a shower or bathe, I use that room.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. I'd love to have a hot spring at my house.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, it's very nice. It's very, very nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Does your house also have a yard?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It kind of has a yard. So outside my house, there's an area for flowers and bushes . And it's like a yard or a garden around the house, but it's not a place you can play sports. There's no grass or anything. So it's a very, very small yard. But, you know, it's a nice place.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh yeah. It sounds like a nice place to live.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is a nice place to live. I'm very, very lucky.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: You said you have a sleeping room, not a bedroom. What does that mean?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I live at a Japanese style house. So it's called the tatami room. And you sleep in the tatami room and you sleep on the floor on a futon. So I don't have a bed. So it's not a bedroom. It's a room that you sit in during the day and you can eat and talk with guests. But it's also a room that you sleep in at night. So yeah, I call it my sleeping room.
But I think in Japan, they just call it the tatami room.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Is it comfortable sleeping on the floor?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, it's really comfortable. Now I love it. So before, I slept on a bed. But now I sleep on the futon on the floor and I really like it. Actually, I prefer to sleep on the futon on the floor.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, it sounds like your house is really comfortable.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is. It is. I never want to leave.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So Meg, do you live in a house or an apartment?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I live in an apartment near the train station.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, you live downtown.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Do you like living downtown?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do like living downtown because it's so convenient. Everything is close by, grocery stores, the mall, the station.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's great. So what about your apartment? Do you have a nice apartment?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It's a nice apartment, but it's really small.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh yeah? How many rooms?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Well, there are three rooms. But each room is pretty small. There's a bedroom, a sitting room like a living room, and the kitchen room.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, wow. So in your bedroom, like, do you have a big queen size bed, a small bed?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have a small twin size bed or a single bed in the bedroom because it's pretty small. So there's not much space for a big bed.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right. So do you have a TV in your bedroom?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No. Actually, I don't own a TV at all.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Really? So there's no TV in the living room, too.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: There's no TV anywhere in the apartment.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow. What do you do in your house?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have a laptop computer. So usually, I can watch some TV shows or videos on my laptop.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right. Okay. Do you like to watch movies in bed?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. Sometimes I like to watch movies in bed or sometimes I prefer to sit in the living room and watch movies.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Right. So you must have high-speed Internet.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do. Yes. I have an Internet box that my laptop can connect to.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Cool. Do you have a nice big sofa?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have two small sofas. So you can push them together to make one big sofa or you can keep them separate . Usually, I keep them separate because there's more room for people to sit on.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Now, you like to cook. So you must have a nice kitchen.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Unfortunately, I have a very tiny kitchen.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh no. How do you cook?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have to use some extra tables to have more space. The counter is really small, so there's not much space. So I have an extra table I use for preparing the food.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Do you have an oven?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have a very small toaster oven. So it's not really an oven.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right. So do you have a microwave?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I do have a microwave and a small refrigerator and one burner, like a stove top burner.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Do you cook every night?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I don't cook every night. Sometimes, I'm too busy. And sometimes because my kitchen is so small, I get a little frustrated . So I just pick up some food from a restaurant.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right. Now, you live in an apartment, so how many floors does your apartment building have?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: The building has five floors and I live on the fifth floor.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Nice. Fifth floor.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. The view is nice, but unfortunately, there's no elevator.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh no.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So you always have to take the stairs.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow. Five flights of stairs .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Five flights of stairs everyday. But it's good exercise.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So you're on the fifth floor. Do you have a balcony?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I have a small balcony where my washing machine is and I can also hang out my laundry out there.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh cool, washing machine is outside.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It is outside. It's a little different from my house in America.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So from your view, what can you see?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I can see the train station from one window and all the restaurants downtown. And from a different window, I can see the mountains.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh nice. Yeah, the mountains are nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, it's really pretty.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Hey, Todd. I know you've traveled a lot. What countries have you lived in?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I've lived in three countries. I've traveled to many, many countries. But I've actually lived in three. I lived in England for one year. I lived in Thailand for four years. And I have lived in Japan for 15 years.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. So when you lived in England, why did you live there?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It was the first country I traveled to after college. And I had a work permit , a work visa for one year. And I worked at a pub restaurant, which was great. It was in the countryside. And I really enjoyed it. And then I did that for six months. I lived near Cambridge. So, I was near Cambridge University. And then after that I moved to London. And again, I worked at a restaurant. And I lived in London and just worked.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. So it was after college. How old were you?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I was 23 years old.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, and living in London. That must have been fun .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It was fun. And interestingly , when I went to England, I could not speak English. So, I could not understand British people. It took me maybe two months before I could understand their English. So it was very, very difficult to understand British people when I first moved there.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Ah, so you liked it.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I did like England. It was fun. It was my first country. But the weather was cold for me. I'm from California, and California in the United States is very warm. So I didn't like the weather. But that's okay because all British people don't like the weather, too.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Everybody complains about the weather.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So after England, did you move someplace warmer?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I did. Right after England, I moved to Thailand. And I lived in Thailand for over four years.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Wow. Why did you live in Thailand?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I was traveling. And in Thailand I had no money and I needed a job. And I wanted to stay in Thailand, so I became an English teacher.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Really?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Did you teach English there for four years?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I did. So I went there and I began teaching English. Then I got a teaching course certificate to teach English in Thailand, and I really enjoyed it. The Thai students were really fun. And Thailand is a great place to live because the weather is really nice. The people are really friendly and the food is delicious. It has the best food in the world, I think.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I've also heard that Thailand is beautiful. Is it true?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: It is. It has many, many beautiful islands and it has lots of beautiful places with nature and the mountains. It has jungles. It has beautiful beaches. So it's a nice place to live.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So you like Thailand, too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: I did. Thailand was great. Yeah.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: So England, Thailand, you said next was Japan?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, so next was Japan. And Japan is nice. I am a teacher, an English teacher in Japan and I love teaching English in Japan. Like Thailand, the food is really, really good. The people are nice. The scenery is really beautiful. So Japan is really nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Are there fun things to do in Japan?

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yes. Actually, I like Japan the most because you get everything. You get lots of beautiful nature. So, you can go hiking. You can go see beautiful beaches. You can go to really nice islands. But also Japan has many, many nice cities. So you can go to Tokyo, Osaka, Fukuoka and the cities have lots to do. There's good shopping, great restaurants. It's easy to travel in Japan by train and bus. So, it's really nice.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Oh, that sounds like the best of both worlds .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah, it is. Definitely a good place to live.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Hey, Meg. We are talking about traveling and visiting other countries. What countries have you traveled to?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I've been to quite a few different countries. For example, Spain, Belize and Indonesia.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, three different continents .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, pretty far apart.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow, that's cool. So Spain, that must be a really nice country. What did you think of Spain?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Spain is really beautiful. There's a lot of beautiful nature and also some nice cities. While I was there, I lived in a small city called Caceres.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh nice. Are the people really friendly in Spain?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes. Actually, the people are very friendly and very helpful, especially if you're lost.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, that's great. I hear Spanish food is really, really good.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Spanish food is delicious. I lived with a Spanish family and my Spanish mom cooked delicious meals every day for lunch. In Spain, seafood is really popular. So I ate a lot of fish and shrimp.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, I love fish and shrimp .

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Me too.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Now, Spain is really warm, right?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yes. Spain was very hot while I was there during the summer.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh yeah? How hot? How hot does it get?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It got up past 40 Degrees Celsius during the summer.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Wow.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah. It was pretty hot.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Does it rain?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: It does rain. But when I was there in the summer, it didn't rain very often.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So what about Belize? Belize is a really small country.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Belize is very small, but it's also hot similar to Spain in the summer.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Why did you go to Belize?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I went to Belize on a study trip for school, and I stayed there for about two weeks.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Now, does Belize have good food?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Belize also has good food. There was a family that cooked for us and we had a lot of delicious almost Mexican type food.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh really? So for example, what do you eat? Like, what do people eat in Belize?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: People eat – it's kind of like a taco but flat with a tortilla, and some meat and vegetables on top and some spices that make it really delicious.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So the last country is Indonesia. When did you go to Indonesia?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I actually went to Indonesia just last year.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh wow. How long did you stay?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I only stayed there for about a week.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh yeah? Oh, short trip.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, it was a short trip, but I was just visiting some friends there.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Where did you go?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I went to Jakarta and Bali.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, okay. So I hear Bali has really beautiful beaches. Is it true?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Yeah, it's true. There are a lot of famous and beautiful beaches in Bali.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh, did you surf in Bali?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I've never surfed before. Usually, when I went to the beach, I just wanted to put my feet in the water .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh yeah. Now, Bali also has very famous scenery on the inside like the rice fields. Did you see the rice fields of Bali?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: No, I didn't see the rice fields. But I did go to some famous historical spots .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So of the three countries – Spain, Belize and Indonesia – what country was your favorite?

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: Maybe Spain was my favorite because I love learning language and it was really nice to stay with my Spanish family.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. I could see that. I really want to go to Spain, and I hope to go soon.

lines.speaker: Meg
lines.text: I hope you can go too. It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So John, do you like to play golf?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, no. I don't play golf very much, but I play disc golf.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Disc golf? What's that?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, some people call it Frisbee golf. Basically, there are courses at parks. It's similar to golf but the courses are much smaller. You use Frisbees or a flying disc and you have to throw it. So it's different from golf. You're not aiming for a small hole but actually, you need to throw the Frisbee into a basket.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Oh, that sounds fun. Is it very easy?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, it can be easy or it can be very difficult. It depends on the course. Many different parks have different disc golf courses. And you can be an easy beginner or you can be an expert. It all depends on how much you want to get involved .

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: My friends are I, we are beginners, so we just like to have fun. So we just do the easy courses and have a good time. I think it's relaxing.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So you only need one Frisbee?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well actually, it's better to have two or three. You can play with one but in fact, when you learn more about disc golf, there are different sizes and weights of the discs.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Why would you want a different size disc?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, it's similar to the clubs in golf. When you throw you first throw, you want it to go very far, so you should use a heavier disc. But when you're near the basket, you should make a short throw, so you want a lightweight disc.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I see. That's interesting.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Yeah. So as I said, when you want to become an expert, you have to spend more money to get better equipment. It's like any sport, I guess. In fact, they have disc golf competitions now. So you can even participate in a tournament and win some prize money.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Did you ever compete ?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Oh no. I'm just a beginner. I don't think I want to be too serious about it.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So golf has 18 holes. How about disc golf? Does it have 18 holes, too?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Well, not usually. Golf courses are very large, but disc golf courses are usually found in parks. So they usually have only six holes. But you can play 18 holes by doing all 6 three times each.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I see. How do you keep score ?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Score keeping is like real golf. So the winner should have the lowest score. Every time you throw a Frisbee or a flying disc, you have to mark one point. So if you can do a hole in one, that means you can hit the basket on your first try, then you'll only have one point. That's best.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Uh-hmm.

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: But I'm not that good at it. So usually, I have three or four points for each course.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I see. You said disc golf is at the park. Do you have little kids playing in the middle of the course?

lines.speaker: John
lines.text: Sometimes, the kids – of course, they can play wherever they want. And the courses do go though the park where kids play. So we have to be very careful, and we have to use good sportsmanship to wait for the course to be clear.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: It sounds like a lot of fun.

lines.speaker: John

lines.text: Okay. So Sarah, I see you eat soup every day at work. Why are you eating soup every day?

lines.text: That’s because I love to cook soup.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So you cook it and then you just bring it to work everyday?

lines.text: Yeah. I just make a lot on Monday and then I bring it to work everyday of the week.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh nice. So how do you make the soup? What’s your secret?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Well, I like to cook very easy. So I buy meat that’s already cut up, usually, chicken and then some rice, usually brown rice and then I buy some vegetables. So after I bought the ingredients, I chop them up and I put them all together in water until boils and add some seasoning .

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. So you say the water boils, so as soon as the water boils that’s when you put in all the ingredients?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Yes, that’s right.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So you don’t put in the ingredients before the water boils.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: No. I guess, it’s just easier for the water to be hot because then the vegetables and the meat cook a little faster.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: So how do you give the soup flavoring?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I usually add salt and pepper, maybe some garlic. And depending on the type of soup, either maybe some soy sauce or lemon juice.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay. Do you put in the flavoring after you put in the ingredients or before you put in the ingredients?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Maybe after but usually, right about all at the same time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: So I just put everything in at one time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: And then after you cook the soup, do you put the soup in the refrigerator? Do you let it sit outside?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: I usually eat some right then, and I also put it in containers for the week. But I let it sit in the containers out on the counter for a while for it to cool before I put in the refrigerator.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: All right. And so, you don’t put it in the refrigerator until it is cool?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Until it’s about room temperature.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Okay, nice. And then how do you heat it up ? Do you heat it up in a pot or do you heat it up in the microwave?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: In the microwave. It’s the easiest.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Yeah. Nice. So you make enough for five meals?

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Maybe, sometimes. If I think I will get tired of eating it during the week then maybe I’ll just make enough for three or four meals. But if it’s some kind that I think is really delicious and I know I want to eat it everyday, then I’ll make a lot.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Well, if that happens, when you make the soup, you can make it for six or seven and give me a bowl.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.text: Okay. I’ll do that next time.

lines.speaker: Todd
lines.text: Oh great. Thanks.
[End of Transcript]
